主要内容: David's Bridal, a wedding dress retailer, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Monday, November 19, 2018, as part of a restructuring deal with its lenders that will reduce its debt by over $400 million. The company stated that its stores will remain open during the restructuring process, and customers can continue shopping in its more than 300 stores. The bankruptcy is part of a broader strategy to restructure the business, with the company anticipating completion of the court-supervised process by early January. David's Bridal also received commitments for $60 million in new debtor-in-possession financing from existing lenders, along with a recommitment of its existing $125 million asset-backed loan. The bankruptcy reflects broader challenges in the wedding industry, including shifting consumer preferences and the rise of online retailers offering non-traditional wedding attire options. The company acquired digital gift company Blueprint Registry in the summer of 2018 to bolster its online presence, but traditional retailers face difficulties in building the infrastructure needed to support e-commerce expansion. This comes a year after bridal store Alfred Angelo liquidated its business, highlighting the sector's struggles with evolving consumer trends and financial pressures.
